title: Cloud, serverless, configuration, and deployment boundaries
sources: Python documentation: os environment, logging, and configuration concepts
Python Packaging User Guide: build/distribution and dependency concepts
masterChecklist: Cloud and serverless concepts: storage, databases, queues, functions, identity, configuration
Configuration, logging, tests, packaging, documentation, operational handover
Deployment, containers, CI/CD concepts, release safety, monitoring, rollback
whyItMatters: Moving a Python program from a laptop to a hosted service changes its assumptions: configuration is external, instances can restart, storage may be remote, requests may be retried, and observability/rollback become part of the product.
simpleExplanation: Cloud is a delivery model for compute, storage, databases, queues, and identity services. Serverless functions run short pieces of code in response to events but still need clear configuration, timeout, retry, data, and permission rules. Keep application logic separate from deployment-specific configuration so it can be tested locally.
mentalModel: A cloud deployment is a rented kitchen, not your home kitchen. You bring a clear recipe and ingredients list, but the room can be replaced between shifts. Important state belongs in the right durable store, not on one temporary counter.
outcomes: Separate code defaults from environment configuration and secrets.
Choose durable storage/queue boundaries for stateful work.
Plan timeouts, retries, permissions, logging, and rollback before deployment.
Test deployment configuration parsing locally without using a cloud account.

realWorldExample.scenario: A progress-import API is deployed as a short-lived function.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: It stores the import file in temporary local memory, assumes one invocation, logs credentials, and retries an upload without a duplicate key.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Validate configuration at startup, keep durable data in an appropriate managed store, use least-privilege identity, set timeout/retry/idempotency policy, log safe run context, and define a rollback/deployment health check.

explanation: The function receives an environment mapping, making configuration behavior testable without changing the real process environment.
The required storage name is validated rather than silently falling back to an unsafe local default.
Secrets are intentionally not printed or placed in this example; a production deployment uses its approved secret/identity mechanism.
The configuration value alone does not create storage. An outer adapter connects to the selected service with least privilege.
Serverless/container platform details differ, so timeout, concurrency, and retry settings must be checked against the actual deployment platform.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Remove PROGRESS_STORAGE and observe the explicit startup failure. Explain why failing early can be safer than writing production data to an unexpected local path.

procedure: List configuration, secrets, durable state, external dependencies, timeout, retry, and permission needs.
Validate required configuration at startup and keep secrets out of source/control-plane logs.
Treat local process memory/files as temporary unless the selected platform explicitly guarantees otherwise.
Make event/request handlers idempotent where retry or duplicate delivery is possible.
Set bounded timeouts and resource/concurrency limits; define failure and dead-letter/review paths where applicable.
Use least-privilege identity for storage, queue, database, and deployment operations.
Deploy through a repeatable build/release process with health evidence, monitoring, and rollback instructions.

commonMistakes.mistake: Saving important state only in a function/container local file.
commonMistakes.why: Instances can be replaced and local storage may be temporary or non-shared.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use a durable storage boundary appropriate to the data.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting credentials in environment dumps or debug logs.
commonMistakes.why: Deployment logs/configuration can be widely retained or visible.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use approved secret/identity mechanisms and redact logs.

commonMistakes.why: Events/requests can be delivered more than once around failures.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use idempotency keys and durable state transitions.

lab.title: Validate deployment configuration locally
lab.safety: Uses a local dictionary only. It does not read real secrets, modify environment variables, deploy code, or access cloud services.
lab.starterCode:
def load_config(environment):
    # Require PROGRESS_STORAGE and return a safe small config.
    pass

# Add one valid and one missing-setting check.
guidedSteps: Read a required value from the passed mapping.
Reject a missing/blank value with a clear message.
Return only non-secret values needed by the app.
Explain which deployment fact must be verified on the chosen platform.
checks: Uses an injected mapping for deterministic tests.
lab.solutionExplanation: The app validates the contract it needs without coupling the core rule to one cloud provider. A real deployment still needs platform-specific review of identity, timeout, storage durability, retries, and monitoring.
challenges: Predict the risk of a local-file fallback in a replaced container.
Find the secret leak: printing the entire environment for debugging.
Experiment: add a non-secret timeout setting with a documented allowed range.

projectConnection.milestone: Create a local configuration contract, identify durable state and retry keys, document least-privilege/timeout/rollback requirements, and run the configuration lab before selecting a host.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: The project separates code from configuration, avoids local-only state assumptions, documents retry/durability/security decisions, and has a release/rollback checklist.

assessment.question: Why treat function/container local files as temporary?
assessment.answer: Hosted instances can restart, be replaced, or not share local storage with other instances.
assessment.explanation: Durable data needs a deliberate storage boundary.

assessment.question: Why validate configuration at startup?
assessment.answer: The service fails clearly before processing data with missing or unsafe assumptions.
assessment.explanation: It is easier to diagnose than a later partial failure.

assessment.question: Why is idempotency relevant to cloud/serverless events?
assessment.answer: Retries or delivery behavior can run the same intended action more than once.
assessment.explanation: Duplicate-safe state/effects prevent accidental repeated work.
